chapter: Pelican Hall and the Black Diamonds contest
title: Winning the band contest with Armstrong record numbers
summary: He recounts the contest against the Silvertone band and how his band won by playing Louis Armstrong numbers learned from records.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: That's when he made up the band on the Pelican. Well I can give you some of the names of the men's. During that night when we had that band contest, well that didn't have, Black Happy on drum, and Bay Bay originally we had a boy by the name of Bat Brown on trumpet and Shot Madison. He got his picture in the other right. They was on the trumpet and some of the sax section. We had Joe Watkins on clarinet in sax. They used to play with the Si Morgan band too, Joe Watkins. Not Joe Watkins, the drummer.

He lived down there on Falstall in Dauphin. And you see now we had this fella by the name of his name, he was from St. Louis, that guy name is, he used to like to dance, but he was a crack saxophone and a ranger. That guy's name was, but now he was playing with that boy. But anyhow, when they played, everybody we just kept playing. We start off with cornered chops series. And when we played that number, the house, just scream and holler. Right now, if we left it, we'd still be playing. They wouldn't allow the other band to chant, so we had a little short fella. Well, you're doing that.
In other words, you won the concert. We won the concert by playing all them record numbers. I can understand.

You know, it's a terrible thing of a band rehearsal. Every day for a whole week, get them numbers off the record. You play the record. And we didn't have no tapes like y'all got. No, no. We had to play the record and then stop it. Then watch, most of them horns. Right, yeah. To get them horns to get together, you see, and them pianos. And then lots of them things I had to watch for them drum bricks. Then we'd work on the rhythm section. But the main thing they were, they was featuring that cornet and that trombone and Paul on that E-flat out those sax. Yeah. Big Head A. Johnson on a tenor sax. That was the band. And we saw the playing there. And then they screamed. Then we were whistling and screaming and hollering. Then we went in some of them other numbers. All the Louis Armstrongs were coming up those small time records called the OKEH Records. Yeah, yeah. Some of them numbers were taken though. Oh, yeah. Not the big album like we got now.
That's the Hot Five things. Right.

Taken from that section. That's why we took the house that night. So that little fella by the name, he used to be like a floor walker for the Pelican. He went back up to New York. He said, I'm trying to make the review of it, I can't think of them guys' names. But anyhow, he had to go, Shoyman I think, no, no, that man's name is not Shoyman. But he had to get on the floor and beg the people to stop playing, get a lot of other bands a chance to play.
When they finally let them play there?
Yeah, they played a number then. You know, each band's supposed to play, right across the way from one hand. One number each.
